title: Curation Lab: Model Match & Bench Review
next_steps: Send trimmed benchmark spreadsheet and runbook
Provision trial Dedicated pool for 2-week pilot
Schedule SOC2/security deep dive with Security team
Share pricing tiers and estimated cost model
action_items: Lena Park: Share benchmark CSV + runbook; due 2025-09-19
Marcus Ito: Spin up a sample Dedicated profile and populate compatibility matrix; due 2025-09-22
Priya Shah: Provide 3 representative prompts and token distribution; due 2025-09-19
Daniel Cho: Confirm VPC peering requirements and firewall egress rules; due 2025-09-24
summary: Short hands-on demo of the model catalog and benchmarking workflow within the Redwood Console and Optimize toolkit. Focus: how to pick open models for Nebula's analytics assistant, run comparative latency/cost benches, and understand hardware compatibility matrix for a pilot. Agreement to run a 2-week dedicated pilot and follow up on SOC2 docs.
transcript:
00:00 Lena Park: okay everyone were on, thanks for joining the curation lab today. Im Lena from Redwood, AE. Marcus is our SE, and Samir from product will chime in on the catalog heuristics.
00:12 Priya Shah: thanks Lena. Were excited to see how Redwood makes open models usable at scale — weve been playing with a few forks of bloom and llama but hit weird latencies.
00:22 Marcus Ito: yeah, quick note — well walk the Console model catalog, then show Optimize suggestions for batching/quant, and finally run a short bench using your sample prompts if time permits.
00:35 Daniel Cho: timeline wise were looking at an internal pilot in Oct, must fit within our VPC constraints and meet SOC2 controls. Also cost is a big gating factor.
00:48 Lena Park: understood. For the pilot we usually recommend Dedicated, but well show cost/latency tradeoffs for hosted variants too.
00:58 Samir Gupta: small thing — when youre looking at the catalog UI, you can filter by model license, quantization-friendly flag, and hardware compatibility. We surface a compatibility matrix per model so you dont guess whether it will run on A100 v2 vs T4.
01:12 Priya Shah: love that — can you show how you surface actual bench numbers?
01:18 Marcus Ito: sure. Jumping into the Console now — apologies for the screen flip. (screen) Heres the model catalog. Notice the left facets: architecture, license, tokens/sec profile, and recommended quant profiles.
01:36 [Marcus shares link: https://redwood.example/deck/model-catalog - note: internal demo link]
01:40 Marcus Ito: Im opening the model detail for "LlamaX-7B-open" — youll see microbenchmarks for p50/p95 latency at different sequence lengths and a cost estimate per 1M tokens on hosted vs dedicated.
01:55 Ava Brooks: Im seeing numbers but are those measured on your runtime or from upstream community runs?
02:01 Marcus Ito: theyre measured on Redwood runtime with the model compiled to our optimized kernels. We also annotate community-reported results when available but mark them as external.
02:12 Daniel Cho: can we re-run those benches with our prompts?
02:16 Marcus Ito: yes — thats where the Optimize toolkit comes in. You upload a prompt set and we run batched benches across candidate models and hardware configs. It produces a CSV with throughput, avg latency, and token cost.
02:30 Priya Shah: sweet. Show an example?
02:34 Marcus Ito: demo time — Im uploading a small prompt set (sample included) and selecting three candidate models: LlamaX-7B-open, BloomLite-8B, and Mistral-7b-alt. Choosing hardware targets: A100x1, T4x2, and vCPU fallback.
02:52 [short screen lag]
02:55 Marcus Ito: bench started. It will run short passes (simulated warmup, then 100 inferences each). While this runs, notice the compatibility matrix tab — it lists quantization support (int8/4), KV cache memory footprint, and whether we recommend a continuous-batching policy for that model.
03:18 Priya Shah: the KV cache footprint row is really helpful — weve had OOMs on runtime with older caching.
03:25 Marcus Ito: yea, for your 8k context use case we flag models with large KV foot prints and recommend chunked caching or a smaller context window.
03:34 Daniel Cho: curious about the hosted fallback policy — if Dedicated is saturated, do we auto-route to hosted? Any data residency implications?
03:44 Lena Park: routing is policy-driven. You can opt-in to automatic fallback to hosted per-route, but we maintain region constraints so data residency is respected; for strict residency you can disable fallback.
03:58 Ava Brooks: and encryption? KMS?
04:02 Lena Park: private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM. Hosted uses customer-controlled keys for at-rest but managed KMS is also available. Well include the security brief for details.
04:13 [bench finishes, UI updates]
04:16 Marcus Ito: results up — sending to chat. You should see p50/p95 latency and an estimated token cost. For LlamaX on A100 were seeing p50 ~78ms, p95 ~240ms, cost per 1M tokens $85 on dedicated assumptions. BloomLite on T4 is higher latency but lower cost.
04:34 Priya Shah: those numbers look promising — how stable are they for bursty traffic?
04:40 Marcus Ito: we surface error rates and tail latency under burst patterns as part of the bench. Also, Optimize recommends batching window settings — e.g., 15ms batching for throughput-bound routes or disable batching for strict latency SLOs.
04:55 Daniel Cho: any support for custom kernels or mixed-precision to squeeze more perf?
04:59 Marcus Ito: yes, our compilation layer will pick mixed-precision paths and inject quantized kernels where accuracy regressions are within thresholds. We also expose a quant profile you can tweak.
05:10 Priya Shah: what about hallucination/regression monitoring? We need to ensure quality doesnt drop with quantization.
05:17 Samir Gupta: Optimize includes a quality monitor tied to prompt sets. We run evals pre/post quant and flag regressions with diffs; you can set a threshold for auto-rollbacks.
05:26 Ava Brooks: good, that addresses one of our major concerns.
05:30 Lena Park: quick qualification: what SLA do you need for the pilot, and who signs off internally?
05:35 Priya Shah: were fine with a 99.5% availability target for pilot, and CTO + legal need to see SOC2 and contract language.
05:43 Lena Park: great — well follow up with the security pack and a tailored pilot proposal.
05:47 Daniel Cho: can you show the compatibility matrix export? We want to add it to our internal runbook.
05:51 Marcus Ito: exporting now — (exports CSV) sending to chat. It includes model, quant support, recommended hardware shapes, KV cache per seq len, and fallback suggestions.
06:04 [file posted: model-compatibility-nebula.csv]
06:08 Priya Shah: perfect. Couple of fast questions — for the Dedicated trial, what billing commit should we expect? Is there a minimum?
06:16 Lena Park: for trials we can provision a short-term Dedicated pool without a long commit; production Reserved capacity has monthly/annual commits. Well add estimated billing for a 2-week dedicated pilot in the follow-up.
06:28 Ava Brooks: any gotchas around token counting differences between models? We use token-level cost metrics and need consistency.
06:36 Marcus Ito: tokenization differences exist; we normalize costs to our internal token unit and include the tokenizer mapping in the bench CSV. We also include cost-per-input example rows so you can sanity-check.
06:48 [brief cross talk about internal procurement timelines, muted background noise]
06:58 Priya Shah: last item — can Redwood run a side-by-side accuracy/ROUGE or domain-specific metric? We want to ensure the open models match our analytics vocabulary.
07:07 Samir Gupta: yes, bring a labeled eval set and we can run post-quantization evaluations and return a quality report. Thats part of the Optimize flow well run during the pilot.
07:18 Lena Park: OK lets recap. Action items: well send the benchmark CSV, export the compatibility matrix, provision the trial Dedicated profile, and schedule the security deep dive. Priya will send prompts and the eval set.
07:33 Priya Shah: sounds good — thanks everyone.
07:37 Lena Park: thanks all. Ill follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff and security call.
07:44 [end]
